The failing test `testLang865` is calling the method `assertValidToLocale` from `LocaleUtils` class in Apache Commons Lang library. The current bug report mentions that the `LocaleUtils.toLocale` method does not handle strings starting with an underscore as specified in the javadocs of `Locale.toString()`. The fix for a previous ticket did not handle cases like "fr\\_\\_P" properly. 

Looking at the implementation of the `LocaleUtils.toLocale` method, it checks for different cases in the input string to create a `Locale` object. However, the method does not handle the case where the string starts with an underscore properly. This aligns with the reported issue.

To address the bug, the `LocaleUtils.toLocale` method needs to be modified to handle strings starting with an underscore as specified in the javadocs of `Locale.toString()`.

Next, I will provide the best methods to be fixed.
```
org.apache.commons.lang3.LocaleUtils.toLocale(java.lang.String)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
